blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A CI coordinator runs in bypassPermissions, and its reviewer definition lists only the tools Read and Grep. A teammate fears that the reviewer can still do anything, because the mode skips prompts. Which limit remains?

options.says: Ruled out because "A tool you leave out isn't in the subagent's session at all: Claude works without it, with no permission prompt or error."

options.text: The permission mode in its own definition, which overrides the parent's mode entirely
options.says: Ruled out because a definition cannot loosen a bypass parent or override it: "A subagent runs in `bypassPermissions` mode only when the parent session itself does."
A tool that is not in the subagent's session cannot be called, whatever the mode.

options.text: The parent's allowed tools, which cap what the mode may approve
options.says: Ruled out because "allowed_tools does not constrain bypassPermissions".

questions.stem: The final answer of a coordinator paraphrases a subagent's findings and drops the line numbers that the user needs. Which fix fits best?

options.text: Raise the subagent's turn limit by a large margin and rerun it
options.says: Ruled out because the paraphrase happens in the parent, which "may summarize it in its own response".

options.text: Tell the parent to keep the report verbatim, or read the tool result directly
options.says: The parent may summarize, so the words that matter must be kept by instruction or read from the result.

options.text: Remove the return-format line from the brief and let it write freely
options.says: Ruled out because the format line decides what comes back: "The return format tells it what the coordinator will do with the answer."

options.text: Switch the subagent to a larger model with a longer context window
options.says: Ruled out because a larger model does not stop the coordinator from summarizing: "The parent receives the subagent's final report, but may summarize it in its own response."

origin.section: What a subagent has, and what you must put in the brief

questions.stem: Six delegates run side by side, and each asks for approval before reading files, which floods the operator. Which design fits best?

options.text: Take the Read tool out of the definitions of all six delegates
options.says: Ruled out because a subagent without the tool cannot read: "A tool you leave out isn't in the subagent's session at all: Claude works without it".

options.text: Set bypassPermissions in each agent definition of the six delegates
options.says: Ruled out because a definition cannot set bypass: "A subagent runs in `bypassPermissions` mode only when the parent session itself does."

options.text: Run the six one after another instead of side by side
options.says: Ruled out because sequencing independent work costs time: "independent subtasks finish in the time of the slowest one rather than the sum of all of them".

options.text: Answer those lookups once, in a PreToolUse hook or inherited rules
options.says: A hook or inherited rules answer the repeated requests once, in one place.
